passages.text: What then shall we say? Shall we continue in sin so that grace may increase?
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to Christians in Rome.
Paul asks a question.
He says, “What shall we say?”
He asks, “Should we keep on sinning?”
He asks, “Should we do this so that grace may increase?”
passages.original: Τί οὖν ἐροῦμεν ἐπιμένωμεν τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ ἵνα ἡ χάρις πλεονάσῃ

passages.text: Certainly not! How can we who died to sin live in it any longer?
passages.sermon: We have died to sin.\r\nWe cannot continue to live in sin.\r\nIt is impossible for us to remain in sin after dying to it.
passages.original: μὴ γένοιτο οἵτινες ἀπεθάνομεν τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ πῶς ἔτι ζήσομεν ἐν αὐτῇ

passages.text: Or aren’t you aware that all of us who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into His death?
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to Christians who have been baptized.
He asks if they know an important truth.
Everyone who is baptized into Christ Jesus is baptized into His death.
Baptism into Christ means sharing in His death.
passages.original: ἢ ἀγνοεῖτε ὅτι ὅσοι ἐβαπτίσθημεν εἰς Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν εἰς τὸν θάνατον αὐτοῦ ἐβαπτίσθημεν

passages.text: We were therefore buried with Him through baptism into death, in order that, just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, we too may walk in newness of life.
passages.sermon:
We were buried with Christ.
Baptism joined us to His death.
God the Father raised Christ from the dead.
God did this by His glory.
God raised Christ to new life.
We also walk in newness of life.
passages.original: συνετάφημεν οὖν αὐτῷ διὰ τοῦ βαπτίσματος εἰς τὸν θάνατον ἵνα ὥσπερ ἠγέρθη Χριστὸς ἐκ νεκρῶν διὰ τῆς δόξης τοῦ Πατρός οὕτως καὶ ἡμεῖς ἐν καινότητι ζωῆς περιπατήσωμεν

passages.text: For if we have been united with Him like this in His death, we will certainly also be united with Him in His resurrection.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to Christians who have been baptized into Christ Jesus.
Paul says we have been united with Christ in His death.
If we have been united with Christ in His death, we will also be united with Christ in His resurrection.
We will certainly share in Christ’s resurrection.
passages.original: Εἰ γὰρ σύμφυτοι γεγόναμεν τῷ ὁμοιώματι τοῦ θανάτου αὐτοῦ ἀλλὰ καὶ τῆς ἀναστάσεως ἐσόμεθα

passages.text: We know that our old self was crucified with Him so that the body of sin might be rendered powerless, that we should no longer be slaves to sin.
passages.sermon:
We know this truth.
Our old self was crucified with Christ.
God did this so the body of sin would lose its power.
Now we are not slaves to sin anymore.
passages.original: τοῦτο γινώσκοντες ὅτι ὁ παλαιὸς ἡμῶν ἄνθρωπος συνεσταυρώθη ἵνα καταργηθῇ τὸ σῶμα τῆς ἁμαρτίας τοῦ μηκέτι δουλεύειν ἡμᾶς τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ

passages.text: For anyone who has died has been freed from sin.
passages.sermon: Anyone who has died is free from sin.\r\nDeath brings release from sin.\r\nSin no longer controls the person who has died.
passages.original: ὁ γὰρ ἀποθανὼν δεδικαίωται ἀπὸ τῆς ἁμαρτίας

passages.text: Now if we died with Christ, we believe that we will also live with Him.
passages.sermon:
Christ died and rose again.
We died with Christ.
We believe this truth.
We will also live with Christ.
passages.original: Εἰ δὲ ἀπεθάνομεν σὺν Χριστῷ πιστεύομεν ὅτι καὶ συζήσομεν αὐτῷ

passages.text: For we know that since Christ was raised from the dead, He cannot die again; death no longer has dominion over Him.
passages.sermon:
Christ is the Son of God.
God raised Christ from the dead.
We know this is true.
Christ cannot die again.
Death no longer rules over Christ.
passages.original: εἰδότες ὅτι Χριστὸς ἐγερθεὶς ἐκ νεκρῶν οὐκέτι ἀποθνῄσκει θάνατος αὐτοῦ οὐκέτι κυριεύει

passages.text: The death He died, He died to sin once for all; but the life He lives, He lives to God.
passages.sermon:
Jesus Christ died.
He died to sin.
He died once for all people.
Now Jesus Christ lives.
He lives to God.
passages.original: ὃ γὰρ ἀπέθανεν τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ ἀπέθανεν ἐφάπαξ ὃ δὲ ζῇ ζῇ τῷ Θεῷ

passages.text: So you too must count yourselves dead to sin, but alive to God in Christ Jesus.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to Christians in Rome.
Paul teaches about Jesus Christ.
Jesus Christ died for sin once for all.
God raised Jesus Christ from the dead.
Jesus now lives to God forever.
You are united with Christ Jesus.
You must think of yourselves as dead to sin.
You must think of yourselves as alive to God.
You are alive to God because you are in Christ Jesus.
passages.original: οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς λογίζεσθε ἑαυτοὺς εἶναι νεκροὺς μὲν τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ ζῶντας δὲ τῷ Θεῷ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ

passages.text: Therefore do not let sin reign in your mortal body so that you obey its desires.
passages.sermon:
Sin is a power that seeks to control people.
Your body is mortal.
Do not let sin rule in your mortal body.
Do not obey the desires of sin.
passages.original: Μὴ οὖν βασιλευέτω ἡ ἁμαρτία ἐν τῷ θνητῷ ὑμῶν σώματι εἰς τὸ ὑπακούειν ταῖς ἐπιθυμίαις αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Do not present the parts of your body to sin as instruments of wickedness, but present yourselves to God as those who have been brought from death to life; and present the parts of your body to Him as instruments of righteousness.
passages.sermon:
Do not give any part of your body to sin.
Do not use your body to do evil things.
Give yourselves to God.
God has brought you from death to life.
Give every part of your body to God.
Use your body to do what is right for God.
passages.original: μηδὲ παριστάνετε τὰ μέλη ὑμῶν ὅπλα ἀδικίας τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ ἀλλὰ παραστήσατε ἑαυτοὺς τῷ Θεῷ ὡσεὶ ἐκ νεκρῶν ζῶντας καὶ τὰ μέλη ὑμῶν ὅπλα δικαιοσύνης τῷ Θεῷ

passages.text: For sin shall not be your master, because you are not under law, but under grace.
passages.sermon:
Sin will not rule over you.
Sin will not be your master.
You are not under the law.
You are under grace.
passages.original: ἁμαρτία γὰρ ὑμῶν οὐ κυριεύσει οὐ γάρ ἐστε ὑπὸ νόμον ἀλλὰ ὑπὸ χάριν

passages.text: What then? Shall we sin because we are not under law, but under grace? Certainly not!
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to Christians in Rome.
Paul teaches about sin, law, and grace.
Paul asks a question.
He says, “What then?”
He asks, “Should we sin because we are not under law but under grace?”
He answers, “Certainly not!”
passages.original: Τί οὖν ἁμαρτήσωμεν ὅτι οὐκ ἐσμὲν ὑπὸ νόμον ἀλλὰ ὑπὸ χάριν μὴ γένοιτο

passages.text: Do you not know that when you offer yourselves as obedient slaves, you are slaves to the one you obey, whether you are slaves to sin leading to death, or to obedience leading to righteousness?
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to Christians in Rome.
Paul teaches about sin and obedience.
If you offer yourself to obey someone, you become that person's slave.
You are a slave to the one you obey.
If you obey sin, you become a slave to sin.
Sin leads to death.
If you obey, you become a slave to obedience.
Obedience leads to righteousness.
passages.original: οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι ᾧ παριστάνετε ἑαυτοὺς δούλους εἰς ὑπακοήν δοῦλοί ἐστε ᾧ ὑπακούετε ἤτοι ἁμαρτίας εἰς θάνατον ἢ ὑπακοῆς εἰς δικαιοσύνην

passages.text: But thanks be to God that, though you once were slaves to sin, you wholeheartedly obeyed the form of teaching to which you were committed.
passages.sermon:
God deserves thanks.
You were once slaves to sin.
You obeyed the teaching given to you.
You obeyed from your heart.
You committed yourselves to this teaching.
passages.original: χάρις δὲ τῷ Θεῷ ὅτι ἦτε δοῦλοι τῆς ἁμαρτίας ὑπηκούσατε δὲ ἐκ καρδίας εἰς ὃν παρεδόθητε τύπον διδαχῆς

passages.text: You have been set free from sin and have become slaves to righteousness.
passages.sermon:
You were once slaves to sin.
God set you free from sin.
Now you serve righteousness as slaves.
You belong to righteousness.
passages.original: ἐλευθερωθέντες δὲ ἀπὸ τῆς ἁμαρτίας ἐδουλώθητε τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ

passages.text: I am speaking in human terms because of the weakness of your flesh. Just as you used to offer the parts of your body in slavery to impurity and to escalating wickedness, so now offer them in slavery to righteousness leading to holiness.
passages.sermon:
I am speaking in human terms.
I do this because your flesh is weak.
In the past, you offered the parts of your body as slaves to impurity.
You also offered them as slaves to lawlessness.
This led you deeper into lawlessness.
Now, offer the parts of your body as slaves to righteousness.
This leads to holiness.
passages.original: Ἀνθρώπινον λέγω διὰ τὴν ἀσθένειαν τῆς σαρκὸς ὑμῶν ὥσπερ γὰρ παρεστήσατε τὰ μέλη ὑμῶν δοῦλα τῇ ἀκαθαρσίᾳ καὶ τῇ ἀνομίᾳ εἰς τὴν ἀνομίαν οὕτως νῦν παραστήσατε τὰ μέλη ὑμῶν δοῦλα τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ εἰς ἁγιασμόν

passages.text: For when you were slaves to sin, you were free of obligation to righteousness.
passages.sermon: You were once slaves to sin.\r\nAt that time, you did not serve righteousness.\r\nYou had no obligation to righteousness.
passages.original: Ὅτε γὰρ δοῦλοι ἦτε τῆς ἁμαρτίας ἐλεύθεροι ἦτε τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ

passages.text: What fruit did you reap at that time from the things of which you are now ashamed? The outcome of those things is death.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to Christians in Rome.
Paul reminds them of their past life.
You once did things that now make you feel ashamed.
You gained something from those actions.
But what did you really gain?
The result of those actions is death.
passages.original: τίνα οὖν καρπὸν εἴχετε τότε ἐφ’ οἷς νῦν ἐπαισχύνεσθε τὸ γὰρ τέλος ἐκείνων θάνατος

passages.text: But now that you have been set free from sin and have become slaves to God, the fruit you reap leads to holiness, and the outcome is eternal life.
passages.sermon:
You are now free from sin.
God has made you His servant.
You now serve God.
This service produces fruit in your life.
This fruit is holiness.
The result of this holiness is eternal life.
passages.original: νυνὶ δέ ἐλευθερωθέντες ἀπὸ τῆς ἁμαρτίας δουλωθέντες δὲ τῷ Θεῷ ἔχετε τὸν καρπὸν ὑμῶν εἰς ἁγιασμόν τὸ δὲ τέλος ζωὴν αἰώνιον

passages.text: For the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.
passages.sermon:
Sin pays a wage.
The wage of sin is death.
God gives a gift.
God’s gift is eternal life.
God gives this life in Christ Jesus.
Christ Jesus is our Lord.
passages.original: τὰ γὰρ ὀψώνια τῆς ἁμαρτίας θάνατος τὸ δὲ χάρισμα τοῦ Θεοῦ ζωὴ αἰώνιος ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ τῷ Κυρίῳ ἡμῶν
